html:
The Mescalero are an Apache people of south-central New Mexico and west Texas, living around the Sacramento and Sierra Blanca mountains. Their Spanish name comes from mescal, the agave plant they roasted in pits as a main food.

They hunted, gathered and raided across the mountains and the southern plains, and in the 1700s fought both the Comanche and the Spanish. In 1863 the US Army forced them onto the Bosque Redondo reservation alongside their old enemies the Navajo; most Mescalero slipped away in 1865.

The Mescalero Reservation was set up in 1873. In the 1800s and early 1900s it took in other Apache groups, including Lipan and Chiricahua Apache, whose descendants are enrolled in the Mescalero Apache Tribe today.
